subject: Urgent: Zenridge inference latency + 5xx surge (P1)
messages:
From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@zenridge.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: support@zenridge.com, pm@zenridge.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High inference latency and 5xx spike — urgent

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp regression in inference latency and 5xx errors across our production fleet starting ~2029-04-14 02:00 UTC. Symptoms:
- P95 token latency jumped from ~180ms to 600-1200ms for requests routed to us-east-1 hosts.
- 5xx rate reached ~12% during the spikes; overall throughput dropped ~38%.
- Affected routes show intermittent DNS resolution failures and TCP retransmits when calls hit redwood-eu and then fallback paths.

Attached: short packet capture and an error log snippet showing repeated 502/504s with upstream connect timeouts. This is impacting our trading execution customers. We need an immediate P1 bridge and a timeline for mitigation.

Please advise plan/ETA.

Thanks,
Alice Morris
Head of Reliability, Zenridge Financial

Attachments: zenridge_packet_capture.pcap, zenridge_error_log_snippet.txt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: alice.morris@zenridge.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:35:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: High inference latency and 5xx spike — urgent

Alice — thanks for the quick heads up and attachments. I'm escalating this to P1 now and standing up a triage bridge. Initial plan:
1) Open a realtime bridge (link to follow) and capture concurrent traceroutes from a subset of affected hosts.
2) Run targeted DNS timing tests and short-lived redirects to an alternate peering path; if beneficial, we’ll route traffic there.
3) If NAT/port exhaustion on the proxy is present, we'll increase ephemeral port pool and spin additional proxy instances immediately.
4) Keep you updated in 15-minute intervals until stable.

Marissa — can you take the lead on network/peering diagnostics? Tessa, set up a canary reroute to dedicated capacity in us-east-1 and prepare a rollback plan. Vivek, looping you for visibility / exec escalation as needed.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

(Planned bridge: P1 / will share dial-in in next email)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:49:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: High inference latency and 5xx spike — urgent

Quick findings from initial triage (summary):
- Correlation: our monitoring shows repeated BGP route withdraws between us-east-1 and the customer’s VPC peering endpoint starting 2029-04-14 01:58 UTC. We observed route convergence delays on subsequent path selection (~10-40s windows).
- DNS: Zenridge's split-horizon resolver started returning SERVFAILs intermittently; our query latency to their authoritative resolver spiked and retried, adding ~200-400ms per request in some windows. We've seen evidence of rate limiting on their edge resolvers.
- Proxy/NAT: error logs show multiple upstream 502s and 504s; sample from our side indicates exhausted NAT ephemeral ports on a proxy cluster which caused connection queuing and subsequent timeouts.

Sample traceroute snippet (from an affected Redwood host):
 1  10.0.0.1  0.4 ms
 2  100.64.2.53  1.2 ms
 3  198.51.100.37  18.6 ms  << next-hop route change observed
 4  203.0.113.7  220.4 ms  << flapping after 04/14 02:00 UTC

Immediate mitigations applied (15:10 UTC):
- Added temporary static route to force traffic over an alternate peering fabric (reduced observed latency on canary).
- Scaled proxy cluster in us-east-1 + increased NAT ephemeral port pool to mitigate port exhaustion.
- Shortened DNS TTL for our internal service discovery to force re-resolution to stable endpoints; requesting Zenridge to review resolver rate limits.

Recommended next steps:
- Provider: coordinate with interconnect provider to investigate the source of route withdraws and confirm no scheduled maintenance caused this.
- Customer: request a look at resolver logs and whether rate limiting or misconfiguration started 04/14.
- Post-incident: evaluate adding an alternate peer + health-aware routing to avoid single-peering failure modes.

Attaching: route-flap-trace.txt and remediation-runbook.pdf for immediate actions and rollback steps.

Marissa
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: alice.morris@zenridge.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 08:02:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: High inference latency and 5xx spike — urgent

Alice — status update and apologies for the impact.
What we did so far:
- Rerouted a subset of Zenridge traffic over an alternate peering; canary traffic saw p95 drop to ~200ms and 5xx <1% within 12 minutes.
- Scaled dedicated proxy capacity and increased NAT pools; proxy queuing/backpressure reduced.
- Collated packet captures and logs (attached) and shared initial traceroutes with the interconnect provider for deeper analysis.

Ask of Zenridge: if you can share resolver logs or confirm any changes to rate limiting/ACLs on 04/14 that would help pinpoint root cause. Also please run the attached curl test from a representative host and share results.

We will keep the alternate peering in place while we confirm stability and coordinate a permanent fix with the interconnect carrier. I'll schedule a 30-minute exec bridge for 10:30 UTC if that works for your team.

Jonas

Attachments: zenridge_packet_capture.pcap, zenridge_error_log_snippet.txt

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: execs@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec note: Zenridge outage window + next steps

TL;DR — customer-facing production degradation (P95 latency and 5xx spike) was caused by cascading path failures: VPC peering route withdraws -> DNS resolution retries -> proxy NAT exhaustion. Immediate mitigations restored acceptable service for canary traffic; full mitigation in progress.

Impact: Zenridge (high-value finserv customer) experienced ~2.5 hours of degraded throughput and elevated error rates during the peak of the event. Risk: trading customers impacted; potential revenue/SLR exposure.

Action items for leadership:
- Approve immediate outreach credits for impacted period (suggest 10% service credit while root cause validated).
- Prioritize cross-team postmortem and require the network team to produce a remediation timeline (alternate peering, health-aware routing, NAT scaling automation).
- Authorize a short-term increase in interconnect monitoring budget and a partner escalation with the interconnect carrier.

I'll join the postmortem with Zenridge and coordinate final communication.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
